title: Likelihood of Ban on Single-use Plastics for Singapore
what_it_is: Likelihood of Ban on Single-use Plastics for Singapore

sections.label: NEA lifecycle assessment of disposables
sections.summary: NEA's lifecycle assessment found that substituting plastics with other single-use packaging materials is not necessarily better for the environment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: NEA conducted a lifecycle assessment of single-use carrier bags and disposables and found that substituting plastics with other types of single-use packaging materials is not necessarily better for the environment.

sections.label: Mandatory packaging reporting and EPR framework
sections.summary: NEA will require certain companies to report packaging information annually, laying the foundation for an EPR framework by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Moving upstream next year, NEA will require brand owners, manufacturers and importers of packaged goods, as well as supermarkets with an annual turnover exceeding $10 million to report information on the packaging they place on the market and their plans for reducing, reusing or recycling this packaging annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Companies should take action to reduce the amount of packaging used and minimise waste generation at source.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: This will also lay the foundation of an Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework for managing packaging waste, including plastic waste, which NEA will put in place no later than 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: For example, we are working with the industry to tap on the Towards Zero Waste Grant to roll out 50 reverse vending machines this year.

sections.label: Lifecycle assessment on disposable alternatives
sections.summary: The lifecycle assessment study showed replacing single-use plastic bags with other disposables does not necessarily lead to better environmental outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Thirdly, our lifecycle assessment study has actually shown that replacing single-use plastic bags, for instance, with other types of disposables, does not necessarily lead to a better environmental outcome because all types of disposables have environmental impacts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In fact, the British government has estimated that a cotton tote bag would have to be used for 173 times before its greenhouse gas emission impact improves beyond that of the plastic bags that we use to line our bins.

sections.label: UK plastic bag charge outcome
sections.summary: In the UK, the plastic bag charge resulted in an over 80% decline in plastic bag use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the United Kingdom (UK), where they have introduced the plastic bag charge, it resulted in an over 80% decline in the use of plastic bags.

sections.label: Monitoring, campaign, reporting and EPR plans
sections.summary: The Government will monitor developments, strengthen its campaign, put in place mandatory upstream reporting and implement an EPR framework by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As I have said, we will continue to monitor developments on this front.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We have just strengthened our efforts in terms of the campaign as well as we are going to put in place mandatory reporting upstream to remove packaging waste upstream to remove the amount of packaging used and packaging waste generated and then implement an EPR framework, latest by 2025.

sections.label: Public availability of studies
sections.summary: A life cycle assessment study was shared at various opportunities, and the quoted British government study is publicly available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider making public the studies that it is using that lead to such data, the methodology behind those studies, the limitations of those studies and to put that into the public domain, if it has not done so already?

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We have actually shared a life cycle assessment study at various opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The one that I have just quoted is a British government study, which is also available publicly.
